items.ar: قوله: (يَا عِبَادِيَ لَو أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ كَانُوا عَلَى أَتقَى قَلبِ رَجُلٍ وَاحدٍ مِنكُمْ مَا زَادَ ذَلِكَ فِي مُلْكِي شَيْئَاً) يعني لو أن كل العباد من الإنس والجن الأولين والآخرين كانوا على أتقى قلب رجل ما زاد ذلك في ملك الله شيئاً، وذلك لأن ملكه عزّ وجل عام واسع لكل شيء، للتقيّ والفاجر.
items.tr: 'If the first and last of you, humans and jinn, were as God-fearing as the most God-fearing heart among you, it would add nothing to My dominion': even if all servants, humans and jinn (unseen beings), first and last, had that heart, Allah's dominion would not increase. His dominion is universal, encompassing everything, righteous and wicked.

items.ar: ووجه قوله: (مَا زَادَ ذَلِكَ فِي مُلكِي شَيئَاً) أنهم إذا كانوا على أتقى قلب رجل واحد كانوا من أولياء الله، وأولياء الله عزّ وجل جنوده، وجنوده يتسع بهم ملكه،
items.tr: 'It would add nothing to My dominion' is mentioned because, with the most God-fearing heart, they would be Allah's devoted servants, who are His troops, and troops expand dominion.

items.ar: ثم قال: (يَا عِبَادِيَ لَو أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ كَانُوا عَلَى أَفجَرِ قَلبِ رَجُلٍ وَاحدٍ مِنكُمْ مَا نَقَصَ ذَلِكَ مِن مُلْكِي شَيْئَاً) ووجه ذلك: أن الفاجر عدو لله عزّ وجل فلا ينصر الله، ومع هذا لاينقص من ملكه شيئاً لأن الله تعالى غني عنه.
items.tr: Then He says: 'If the first and last of you, humans and jinn, were as wicked as the most wicked heart among you, it would diminish My dominion in no way.' The wicked are Allah's enemies and do not support His cause, yet His dominion is undiminished because He needs none of them.

items.ar: قوله: (يَا عِبَادِيَ لَو أَنَّ أَوَّلَكُمْ وَآخِرَكُمْ وَإِنْسَكُمْ وَجِنَّكُمْ قَامُوا في صَعِيدٍ وَاحِدٍ فَسَأَلونِي فَأَعطَيتُ كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ مَسأَلَتَهُ) أي إذا قاموا في أرض واحدة منبسطة، وذلك لأنه كلما كثر الجمع كان ذلك أقرب إلى الإجابة.
items.tr: 'If the first and last of you, humans and jinn, stood in one place and asked Me, and I granted each his request': on one flat stretch of land, because the larger the gathering, the closer it is to having supplication answered.

items.ar: قوله: (مَا نَقَصَ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا عِنْدِي إِلاَّ كَمَا يَنْقُصُ المِخْيَطُ إذَا أُدْخِلَ البَحرَ) وهذا من باب المبالغة في عدم النقص، لأن كل واحد يعلم أنك لو أدخلت المخيط وهو الإبرة الكبيرة في البحر ثم أخرجتها فإنها لا تنقص البحر شيئاً ولا تغيره، (يَا عِبَادِيَ إِنَّمَا هِيَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ) هذه جملة فيها حصر طريقه: (إنما) أي ما هي إلا أعمالكم أُحْصِيْهَا لَكُمْ أي أضبطها تماماً بالعدّ لا زيادة ولا نقصان، لأنهم كانوا في الجاهلية لا يعرفون الحساب فيضبطون الأعداد
items.tr: 'That would diminish what I possess only as a needle diminishes the sea when dipped into it' emphatically expresses no diminution. Everyone knows that dipping a large needle into the sea and withdrawing it neither diminishes nor changes the sea. 'My servants, it is only your deeds': innama expresses restriction, only your deeds. 'I count them for you': record them precisely, without addition or subtraction. In the pre-Islamic period, they did not know calculation, so they kept track of numbers.

items.ar: قوله: (ثُمَّ أُوَفِّيكُمْ إِيَّاهَا) أي في الدنيا والآخرة، وقد يكون في الدنيا فقط، وقد يكون في الآخرة فقط.
items.tr: 'Then repay you in full for them': in this world and the Hereafter, or perhaps in this world alone or the Hereafter alone.

items.ar: فالتوفيه تكون في الدنيا دون الآخرة للكافر، أما المؤمن فتكون في الدنيا والآخرة جميعاً، أو في الآخرة فقط.
items.tr: For the disbeliever, full payment is in this world, not the Hereafter. For the believer, it is in both or in the Hereafter alone.

items.ar: قوله: ( فَمَنْ وَجَدَ خَيْرَاً فَليَحْمَدِ اللهَ) أي من وجد خيراً من أعماله فليحمد الله على الأمرين: على توفيقه للعمل الصالح، وعلى ثواب الله له.
items.tr: 'Whoever finds good should praise Allah': praise Him for two things, enabling the righteous deed and rewarding it.

items.ar: قوله: (وَمَنْ وَجَدَ غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ) أي وجد شراً أو عقوبة (فَلا يَلُومَنَّ إِلاَّ نَفسَهُ) لأنه لم يُظلم، واللوم: أن يشعر الإنسان بقلبه بأن هذا فعل غير لائق وغير مناسب، وربما ينطق بذلك بلسانه.
items.tr: 'Whoever finds otherwise': evil or punishment, 'should blame no one but himself,' because he was not wronged. Blame is inward recognition that an act was improper or unsuitable, perhaps also expressed verbally.

items.ar: قال ابن كثير رحمه الله: "هُوَ أَوَّلُ مَنْ حَيَّا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بِتَحِيَّةِ الْإِسْلَامِ، ثُمَّ رَجَعَ إِلَى بِلَادِهِ وَقَوْمِهِ، فَكَانَ هُنَاكَ حَتَّى هَاجَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ، فَهَاجَرَ بَعْدَ الْخَنْدَقِ، ثُمَّ لَزِمَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ حَضَرًا وَسَفَرًا، وَرَوَى عَنْهُ أَحَادِيثَ كَثِيرَةً"،وكان رسول الله ﷺ يحبه، ويعتني بأمره، ويرشده إلى ما يصلحه:عَنْ أَبِي ذَرٍّ، أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ، قَالَ: (يَا أَبَا ذَرٍّ، إِنِّي أَرَاكَ ضَعِيفًا، وَإِنِّي أُحِبُّ لَكَ مَا أُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِي، لَا تَأَمَّرَنَّ عَلَى اثْنَيْنِ، وَلَا تَوَلَّيَنَّ مَالَ يَتِيمٍ).
items.tr: Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said: He was the first to greet Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, with Islam's greeting, then returned to his country and people until Allah's Messenger emigrated to Madinah. He emigrated after Al-Khandaq, then remained with Allah's Messenger at home and on journeys, narrating many hadiths. Allah's Messenger loved him, cared for him and guided him to what benefited him. Abu Dharr reported that Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Abu Dharr, I see you as weak, and I love for you what I love for myself. Do not take command over two people or manage an orphan's wealth.

items.ar: قوله: (أَنَ أُنَاسَاً) هؤلاء هم الفقراء قالوا للنبي ﷺ (ذَهَبَ أَهلُ الدثورِ) أي الأموال الكثيرة (بِالأُجورِ) أي الثواب عليها، وليس قصدهم بذلك الحسد، ولا الاعتراض على قدر الله، لكن قصدهم لعلهم يجدون أعمالاً يستطيعونها يقومون بها تقابل ما يفعله أهل الدثور.
items.tr: 'Some people': these were poor people. They told the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, 'The wealthy,' those with much wealth, 'have taken the rewards.' They intended neither envy nor objection to Allah's decree, but hoped to find deeds within their ability matching what the wealthy did.

items.ar: قوله: (يُصَلونَ كَمَا نُصَلي،وَيَصومُونَ كَمَا نَصوم، وَيَتَصَدَّقونَ بِفُضولِ أَموَالِهم) يعني ولا نتصدق لأنه ليس عندنا شيء، فكيف يمكن أن نسبقهم أو نكون مثلهم، هذا مراد الصحابة رضي الله عنهم وليس مرادهم قطعاً الاعتراض على قدر الله عزّ وجل، ولا أن يحسدوا هؤلاء الأغنياء.
items.tr: His words, 'They pray as we pray, fast as we fast, and give charity from their surplus wealth,' mean: we do not give charity because we have nothing, so how can we surpass them or be like them? This is what the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, meant. They certainly did not mean to object to Allah's decree or envy those rich people.

items.ar: قال النبي ﷺ: (أَوَلَيسَ قَد جَعَلَ اللهُ لَكُم مَا تَصَّدَّقونَ بِهِ)؟
items.tr: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Has Allah not provided you with things to give in charity?'

items.ar: الجواب: بلى، ثم بيّنَ لهم فقال: (إِنَ بِكُلِّ تَسبيحَه صَدَقَةً) أي إذا قلت: سبحان الله فهي صدقة.
items.tr: The answer is yes. He then explained: 'Every tasbih (saying Subhan Allah) is charity.' If you say, 'Glory be to Allah,' it is charity.

items.ar: قوله: (وَبِكُلِّ تَكبيرَةٍ صَدَقَةً) إذا قلت الله أكبر فهذه صدقة.
items.tr: His words, 'Every takbir (saying Allahu akbar) is charity': if you say, 'Allah is the Greatest,' this is charity.

items.ar: قوله: (وَبِكُلِّ تَحميدَه صَدَقَةً) إذا قلت الحمد لله فهذه صدقة.
items.tr: His words, 'Every tahmid (saying al-hamdu lillah) is charity': if you say, 'Praise be to Allah,' this is charity.

items.ar: قوله: ( وَبِكُلِّ تَهليلَه صَدَقَة) إذا قلت لا إله إلا الله فهي صدقة.
items.tr: His words, 'Every tahlil (saying la ilaha illa Allah) is charity': if you say, 'There is no god worthy of worship except Allah,' it is charity.

items.ar: قوله: ( وَأَمرٌ بِالمَعروفِ صَدَقَةٌ) إذا أمرت من رأيته مقصراً في شيء من الطاعات فهي صدقة.
items.tr: His words, 'Enjoining what is right is charity': if you tell someone whom you see falling short in an act of obedience to do it, this is charity.

items.ar: قوله: (وَنَهيٌ عَن مُنكَرٍ صَدَقَةٌ) إذا رأيت شخصاً على منكر ونهيته فهي صدقة.
items.tr: His words, 'Forbidding what is wrong is charity': if you see someone doing something wrong and forbid him, this is charity.

items.ar: هذه الأشياء التي ذكرها النبي ﷺ وقال: إنها صدقة يستطيعها هؤلاء الفقراء.
items.tr: These things that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, described as charity are within the ability of these poor people.

items.ar: والأغنياء يمكن أن لا يتصدقون كل يوم، وإذا تصدقوا باليوم لا يستوعبون اليوم بالصدقة، فأنتم قادرون على هذا.
items.tr: The rich may not give charity every day, and even when they do, their giving does not occupy the entire day. You are capable of doing this.

items.ar: ولما قرر النبي ﷺ هذا اقتنعوا رضي الله عنهم لكن لما قال: (وَفي بُضعِ أَحَدِكُم صَدَقَةٌ) أي أن الرجل إذا أتى أهله فله بذلك صدقة، قالوا: يا رسول الله أيأتي أحدنا شهوته ويكون له فيها أجر؟ استفهاماً وليس اعتراضاً، لكن يريدون أن يعرفوا وجه ذلك، كيف يأتي الإنسان أهله وشهوته ويقال إنك مأجور؟! أي أن الإنسان قد يستبعد هذا ولكن النبي ﷺ بيَّن لهم وجه ذلك فقال: (أَرَأيتُم لو وَضَعَها في حَرَامٍ أَكَانَ عَليهِ وِزر؟) والجواب: نعم يكون عليه وزر لو وضعها في حرام.
items.tr: When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, explained this, they were convinced, may Allah be pleased with them. But when he said, 'In the sexual intercourse of any one of you there is charity,' meaning that a man receives the reward of charity when he has intercourse with his wife, they asked: 'Messenger of Allah, can one of us satisfy his desire and receive a reward for it?' This was a question, not an objection. They wanted to understand how a person could have intercourse with his wife and satisfy his desire yet be told he was rewarded. A person might consider this unlikely, but the Prophet explained it: 'Tell me, if he satisfied it unlawfully, would he bear a sin?' The answer is yes: he would bear a sin if he satisfied it unlawfully.

items.ar: قال ﷺ (فَكَذَلِكَ إِذَا وَضَعَها في الحَلالِ كَانَ لَهُ أَجرٌ) فاستغنى عن الحرام فكان مأجوراً بهذا، وهذا ما يسمى عند العلماء بقياس العكس، أي إذا ثبت هذا ثبت ضده في ضده.
items.tr: He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'Likewise, if he satisfies it lawfully, he receives a reward.' He thereby dispenses with what is unlawful and is rewarded for this. Scholars call this qiyas al-aks (inverse analogy): if a ruling is established for one thing, the opposite ruling is established for its opposite.

items.ar: بو ذر الغفاري، رضي الله عنه: المشهور أن اسمه: جندب بن جنادة بن قيس بن عمرو بن مليل بن صعير بن حرام بن عفان.
items.tr: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him: his name is commonly given as Jundub ibn Junadah ibn Qays ibn Amr ibn Mulayl ibn Suayr ibn Haram ibn Affan.

items.ar: السلامى هي المفاصل، وقيل:العظام، والمعنى واحد لا يختلف، لأن كل عظم مفصول عن الآخر بفاصل فإنه يختلف عنه في الشكل، وفي القوة، وفي كل الأمور وهذا من تمام قدرة الله عزّ وجل.
items.tr: Sulama means joints; it has also been said to mean bones. The meaning is the same, with no difference, because every bone is separated from the next by a joint and differs from it in shape, strength, and every other respect. This is part of the perfection of Allah's power.

items.ar: وجاء في صحيح مسلم أن السلامى ثلاثمائة وستون مفصلاً، هكذا جاء في الحديث، والطب الحديث يوافق هذا - سبحان الله - مما يدل على أن رسالة النبي ﷺ حق.
items.tr: Sahih Muslim states that there are three hundred and sixty joints. This is what the hadith says, and modern medicine agrees with it. Glory be to Allah! This is among the indications that the Prophet's message is true.

items.ar: وقوله: (كُلُّ سُلامَى مِنَ النَّاسِ عَلَيْهِ صَدَقَةٌ) والمعنى: كل مفصل عليه صدقة.
items.tr: His words, 'Every joint of a person owes charity,' mean that charity is due for every joint.

items.ar: وقوله: (كُلُّ يَومٍ تَطْلُعُ فِيْهِ الشَّمسُ) يعني كل يوم يصبح على كل عضو من أعضائنا صدقة، أي ثلاثمائة وستون في اليوم، فيكون في الأسبوع ألفين وخمسمائة وعشرين.
items.tr: His words, 'Every day on which the sun rises,' mean that each morning charity is due for every part of our bodies: three hundred and sixty each day, making two thousand five hundred and twenty in a week.

items.ar: لكن من نعمة الله أن هذه الصدقة عامة في كل القربات، فكل القربات صدقات، وهذا شيء ليس بصعب على الإنسان.
items.tr: But by Allah's grace this charity includes all acts that draw one closer to Him. All such acts are charity, and this is not difficult for a person.

items.ar: ثم قال: (تَعْدِلُ بَينَ اثنَيْنِ صَدَقَة) تعدل أي تفصل بينهما إما بصلح وإما بحكم، والأولى العدل بالصلح إذا أمكن ما لم يتبين للرجل أن الحكم لأحدهما، فإن تبين أن الحكم لأحدهما حرم الصلح، وهذا قد يفعله بعض القضاة، يحاول أن يصلح مع علمه أن الحق مع المدعي أو المدعى عليه، وهذا محرم لأنه بالإصلاح لابد أن يتنازل كل واحد عما ادعاه فيحال بينه وبين حقه.
items.tr: He then said: 'Acting justly between two people is charity.' Acting justly means settling their dispute, either through reconciliation or a judgment. Reconciliation is preferable when possible, unless it becomes clear that the ruling belongs to one of them. If that is clear, reconciliation is forbidden. Some judges may try to bring about a settlement while knowing that the right belongs to the claimant or the defendant. This is forbidden because a settlement necessarily requires each to relinquish something he claims, thereby preventing him from obtaining his right.

items.ar: قوله: (وَتُعِيْنُ الرَّجُلَ فِي دَابَّتِهِ) أي بعيره مثلاً "تَحْمِلُهُ عَلَيْهَا" إذا كان لايستطيع أن يركب تحمله أنت وتضعه على الرحل هذا صدقة "أَو تَحْمِلُ لَهُ عَلَيْهَا مَتَاعَهُ" متاعه ما يتمتع به في السفر من طعام وشراب وغيرهما، تحمله على البعير وتربطه، هذا صدقة.
items.tr: His words, 'Helping a man with his mount,' mean his camel, for example. 'Lifting him onto it': if he cannot mount it, you lift him and place him on the saddle; this is charity. 'Or lifting his belongings onto it for him': his belongings are what he uses on his journey, such as food, drink, and other things. Loading them onto the camel and securing them is charity.

items.ar: قوله: (وَالكَلِمَةُ الطَّيِّبَةُ صَدَقَةٌ) أي كلمة طيبة سواء طيبة في حق الله كالتسبيح والتكبير والتهليل، أو في حق الناس كحسن الخلق صدقة.
items.tr: His words, 'A good word is charity,' mean any good word, whether concerning Allah, such as tasbih (glorifying Allah), takbir (declaring Allah's greatness), and tahlil (declaring His oneness), or concerning people, such as good manners. It is charity.

items.ar: قوله: (وَبِكُلِّ خُطوَةٍ تَخْطُوهَا إِلَى الصَّلاةِ صَدَقَة) سواء بعدت المسافة أم قصرت، وإذا كان قد تطهر في بيته وخرج إلى الصلاة لايخرجه إلا الصلاة لم يخط خطوة إلا رفع الله له بها درجة، وحطّ عنه بها خطيئة.
items.tr: His words, 'Every step you take toward prayer is charity,' apply whether the distance is long or short. If a person purifies himself at home and goes out solely to pray, for every step he takes Allah raises him one degree and removes one sin.

items.ar: فيكتسب شيئين: رفع الدرجة، وحطّ الخطيئة.
items.tr: He thus gains two things: elevation in rank and removal of a sin.

items.ar: قوله: (وَتُمِيطُ الأذَى عَنِ الطَّرِيْقِ صَدَقَةٌ) أي تزيل الأذى وهو ما يؤذي المارة من حجر أو زجاج أو قاذورات فأي شيء يؤذي المارين إذا أميط عن طريقهم فإنه صدقة.
items.tr: His words, 'Removing something harmful from the road is charity,' mean removing anything that harms passersby, such as a stone, glass, or filth. Anything that harms people passing along the road is charity when it is removed from their way.

items.ar: قوله: ( البر) أي الذي ذكره الله تعالى في القرآن فقال (وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى ) والبر كلمة تدل على كثرة الخير.
items.tr:
His statement:  البر [Al-birr (righteousness).] This is what Allah Most High mentions in the Quran, saying: وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى  [Full-verse context (5:2):
O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allāh or [the sanctity of] the sacred month or [neglect the marking of] the sacrificial animals and garlanding [them] or [violate the safety of] those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and [His] approval. But when you come out of iḥrām, then [you may] hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people for having obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām lead you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allāh; indeed, Allāh is severe in penalty.]. Birr is a word indicating abundant goodness.

items.ar: قوله: (حسن الخلق ) أي حسن الخلق مع الله، وحسن الخلق مع عباد الله، فأما حسن الخلق مع الله فان تتلقي أحكامه الشرعية بالرضا والتسليم، وأن لا يكون في نفسك حرج منها ولا تضيق بها ذرعا
items.tr: His words, 'Good character,' mean good character toward Allah and toward Allah's servants. Good character toward Allah means receiving His religious rulings with acceptance and submission, without feeling any inner objection or distress about them.

items.ar: وأيضا حسن الخلق مع الله في أحكامه القدرية وتقوم بما أمرت به وتنزجر عما نهيت عنه.
items.tr: It also means good character toward Allah concerning His decrees, doing what you have been commanded and refraining from what you have been forbidden.

items.ar: أما حسن الخلق مع الناس فقد سبق أنه: بذل الندى وكف الأذى والصبر على الأذى، وطلاقة الوجه.
items.tr: Good character toward people has already been explained: giving generously, refraining from harm, patiently enduring harm, and having a cheerful face.

items.ar: وهذا هو البر والمراد به البر المطلق، وهناك بر خاص كبر الوالدين مثلا وهو الإحسان إليهما بالمال والبدن والجاه وسائر الإحسان.
items.tr: This is birr (righteousness), meaning righteousness in its unrestricted sense. There is also a specific form, such as birr al-walidayn (dutifulness to parents): treating them well with one's wealth, physical effort, influence, and every other kind of kindness.

items.ar: وهل يدخل بر الوالدين في قوله (حسن الخلق)؟
items.tr: Does dutifulness to parents come within his words, 'Good character'?

items.ar: فالجواب: نعم يدخل.
items.tr: The answer is yes, it does.

items.ar: قوله: (والإثم ) هو ضد البر لأن الله تعالى قال: (وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى وَلا تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الإثم وَالْعُدْوَانِ) فما هو الإثم؟
items.tr:
His statement: والإثم  [And al-ithm (sin).] This is the opposite of birr (righteousness), because Allah Most High says: وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى وَلا تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الإثم وَالْعُدْوَانِ [Full-verse context (5:2):
O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of Allāh or [the sanctity of] the sacred month or [neglect the marking of] the sacrificial animals and garlanding [them] or [violate the safety of] those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and [His] approval. But when you come out of iḥrām, then [you may] hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people for having obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Ḥarām lead you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allāh; indeed, Allāh is severe in penalty.]. So what is sin?

items.ar: قوله: (الإثم ما حاك في نفسك) أي تردد وصرت منه في قلق (وكرهت أن يطلع عليه الناس) لأنه محل ذم وعيب، فتجدك مترددا فيه وتكره أن يطلع الناس عليك وهذه الجملة إنما هي لمن كان قلبه صافيا سليما، فهذا هو الذي يحوك في نفسه ما كان إثما ويكره أن يطلع عليه الناس.
items.tr: His words, 'Sin is what wavers within you,' mean that you hesitate over it and become uneasy. 'And you dislike people finding out about it,' because it deserves blame and reproach. You find yourself hesitant about it and dislike people discovering it. This statement concerns a person whose heart is pure and sound. It is such a person who feels inward unease about a sin and dislikes people finding out about it.

items.ar: أما المتمردون الخارجون عن طاعة الله الذين قست قلوبهم فهؤلاء لا يبالون، بل ربما يتبجحون بفعل المنكر والإثم، فالكلام هنا ليس عاما لكل أحد بل هو خاص لمن كان قلبه سليما طاهرا نقيا.
items.tr: As for rebellious people who abandon obedience to Allah and whose hearts have hardened, they do not care; they may even boast of committing wrong and sin. These words therefore do not apply to everyone, but specifically to someone whose heart is sound, pure, and clean.

items.ar: نواس بن سمعان
items.tr: Al-Nawwas ibn Saman

items.ar: نَوَّاسُ بن سِمْعَان بن خالد بن عَمرو بن قُرْط بن عبد اللّه بن أَبي بكر بن كلاب بن ربيعة بن عامر بن صَعْصَعَة العامري الكلابي، معدود في الشاميين.
items.tr: Al-Nawwas ibn Saman ibn Khalid ibn Amr ibn Qurt ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Kilab ibn Rabiah ibn Amir ibn Sasaah al-Amiri al-Kilabi is counted among the people of al-Sham.

items.ar: يقال: إِن أَباه "سِمْعان بن خالد" وفد على النبي صَلَّى الله عليه وسلم، فدعا له، وأَهدى إِلى النبي صَلَّى الله عليه وسلم نعلين، فقبلهما. وزَوَّج أُخته من النبي صَلَّى الله عليه وسلم، فلما دخلت على النبي صَلَّى الله عليه وسلم تَعَوَّذت منه، فتركها وهي الكلابية. وقد اختلفوا في المتعوذة كثيرًا.
items.tr: It is said that his father, Saman ibn Khalid, came as a delegate to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who prayed for him. He presented the Prophet with a pair of sandals, which he accepted. He married his sister to the Prophet, but when she entered his presence she sought refuge from him, so he left her. She was the woman of Kilab. There has been much disagreement about the identity of the woman who sought refuge.

items.ar: روى النوَّاس عن النبي صَلَّى الله عليه وسلم. روى عنه: جُبَير بن نفير، وبُسْر بن عبيد اللّه، وغيرهما.
items.tr: Al-Nawwas narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Jubayr ibn Nufayr, Busr ibn Ubayd Allah, and others narrated from him.

items.ar: وابصة بن معبد
items.tr: Wabisah ibn Mabad

items.ar: وابصة بن معبد بن عتبة بن الحارث بن مالك بن الحارث بن قيس بن كعب بن سعيد بن الحارث بن ثعلبة بن دودان بن أسد بن خزيمة الأسدي وقال أبو حاتم هو وابصة بن عبيدة ومعبد لقب أبو سالم ويقال أبو الشعثاء يقال أبو سعيد وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم سنة تسع وروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم وعن بن مسعود وأم قيس بنت محصن وغيرهم روى عنه ولداه سالم وعمر وزر بن حبيش وشداد مولى عياض وراشد بن سعد وزياد بن أبي الجعد وغيرهم ونزل الجزيرة فروى أبو علي الحراني في تاريخ الرقة من طريق عبيد الله بن عمرو الرقي حدثني أبو عبد الله الرقي وكان من أعوان عمر بن عبد العزيز قال بعث معي عمر بمال وكتب الى وابصة يبعث معي بشرط يكفون الناس عني وقال لا تفرقه الا على نهر جار فاني أخاف أن يعطشوا قال أبو علي ولا أظن هذا الا وهما لأن وابصة ما عاش الى خلافة عمر بن عبد العزيز انتهى وهو كما ظن وقال لعله كان في الأصل ان بن وابصة.
items.tr: Wabisah ibn Mabad ibn Utbah ibn al-Harith ibn Malik ibn al-Harith ibn Qays ibn Kab ibn Said ibn al-Harith ibn Thalabah ibn Dudan ibn Asad ibn Khuzaymah al-Asadi. Abu Hatim said that he was Wabisah ibn Ubaydah, that Mabad was a sobriquet, and that his kunyah (name beginning with Abu) was Abu Salim; Abu al-Shatha and Abu Said are also reported. He came as a delegate to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in the year nine and narrated from him, Ibn Masud, Umm Qays bint Mihsan, and others. His sons Salim and Umar, Zirr ibn Hubaysh, Shaddad the freedman of Iyad, Rashid ibn Sad, Ziyad ibn Abi al-Jad, and others narrated from him. He settled in al-Jazirah. In Tarikh al-Raqqah, Abu Ali al-Harrani related through Ubayd Allah ibn Amr al-Raqqi: Abu Abd Allah al-Raqqi, who was one of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's assistants, told me: 'Umar sent money with me and wrote to Wabisah to send guards with me to keep people away from me. He said: Do not distribute it except beside a flowing river, for I fear they may become thirsty.' Abu Ali said: 'I think this can only be a mistake, because Wabisah did not live until the caliphate of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz.' End quote. It is as he supposed. He said: 'Perhaps the original read: the son of Wabisah.'

items.ar: قوله: (وَعَظَنا) الوعظ:التذكير بما يلين القلب سواء كانت الموعظة ترغيباً أو ترهيباً، وكان النبي ﷺ يتخول أصحابه بالموعظة أحياناً.
items.tr: His words, 'He admonished us': admonition is a reminder that softens the heart, whether by encouragement or warning. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would give his Companions admonition from time to time.

items.ar: وقوله: (وَجلَت مِنهَا القُلُوبُ) أي خافت منها القلوب كما قال الله تعالى: (الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ).
items.tr:
His statement: وَجلَت مِنهَا القُلُوبُ [Hearts trembled because of it.] This means hearts became afraid because of it, as Allah Most High says: الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ [Full-verse context (8:2):
The believers are only those who, when Allāh is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith; and upon their Lord they rely -].

items.ar: ( وَذَرَفَت مِنهَا العُيون) أي ذرفت الدموع، وهو كناية عن البكاء.
items.tr: 'And the eyes shed tears because of it': this means tears flowed, an expression referring to weeping.

items.ar: " فَقُلنَا يَا رَسُول الله:كَأنَّها" أي هذه الموعظة "مَوعِظَةَ مُوَدِِّعٍ" وذلك لتأثيرها في إلقائها،وفي موضوعها،وفي هيئة الواعظ لأن كل هذا مؤثر،حتى إننا في عصرنا الآن تسمع الخطيب فيلين قلبك وتخاف وتبكي، فإذا سمعته مسجلاً لم تتأثر، فتأثير المواعظ له أسباب منها: الموضوع،وحال الواعظ،وانفعاله.
items.tr: 'We said: Messenger of Allah, it is as though this' admonition 'were the admonition of someone bidding farewell.' This was because of the effect of its delivery, its subject, and the preacher's bearing, for all these have an effect. Even today, you may hear a preacher and your heart softens, you become afraid, and you weep, yet hearing him in a recording does not affect you. The effect of admonition has several causes, including the subject, the preacher's condition, and his emotion.

items.ar: قَالَ: (أوصيكُم بِتَقوَى الله عزّ وجل) هذه الوصية مأخوذة من قول الله تعالى: (وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ أَنِ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ) فتقوى الله رأس كل شيء.
items.tr:
He said: أوصيكُم بِتَقوَى الله عزّ وجل [I counsel you to have taqwa (mindfulness) of Allah, mighty and majestic.] This counsel is taken from Allah's statement, Most High: وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ أَنِ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ [Full-verse context (4:131):
And to Allāh belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and yourselves to fear Allāh. But if you disbelieve - then to Allāh belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allāh Free of need and Praiseworthy.]. Taqwa is the foremost matter in everything.

items.ar: ومعنى التقوى: طاعة الله بامتثال أمره واجتناب نهيه على علم وبصيرة.
items.tr: Taqwa (mindfulness of Allah) means obeying Allah by fulfilling His commands and avoiding His prohibitions with knowledge and insight.

items.ar: ولهذا قال بعضهم في تفسيرها: أن تعبد الله على نور من الله، ترجو ثواب الله، وأن تترك ما حرم الله، على نور من الله، تخشى عقاب الله.
items.tr: Thus some have explained it as worshipping Allah in the light of guidance from Him, hoping for His reward, and abandoning what Allah has forbidden in the light of guidance from Him, fearing His punishment.

items.ar: وقال بعضهم:
items.tr: Some have said:

items.ar: خل الذنوب صغيرهاوكبيرها ذاك التقى واعمل كماش فوق أرض الشوك يحذر ما يرى لاتحقرن صغيرة إن الجبال من الحصى
items.tr: Leave sins, small and great: that is taqwa (mindfulness of Allah). Act like someone walking over thorny ground, wary of what he sees. Never belittle a small sin, for mountains are made of pebbles.

items.ar: قوله: (وَالسَّمعُ والطَّاعَة) أي لولاة الأمر بدليل قوله وَإِن تَأمَّر عَليكُم والسمع والطاعة بأن تسمع إذا تكلم، وأن تطيع إذا أمر.
items.tr: His words, 'And hearing and obeying,' concern those in authority, as indicated by 'Even if someone becomes your ruler.' Hearing and obeying mean listening when he speaks and obeying when he commands.

items.ar: قوله: ( وَإن تَأمَّر عَلَيكُم) أي صار أميراً "عبد" أي مملوكاً.
items.tr: His words, 'Even if someone becomes your ruler,' mean becomes your leader, and 'a slave' means someone owned by another.

items.ar: قوله: (فَإِنَّهُ مَن يَعِش مِنكُم) أي تطول به الحياة "فَسَيَرى" والسين هنا للتحقيق اختِلاَفاً كَثيراً في العقيدة، وفي العمل، وفي المنهج، وهذا الذي حصل، فالصحابة رضي الله عنهم الذين عاشوا طويلاً وجدوا من الاختلاف والفتن والشرور ما لم يكن لهم في الحسبان.
items.tr: His words, 'Whoever among you lives,' mean lives a long life. 'Will see' expresses certainty here: much disagreement in belief, action, and method. This is what happened. The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, who lived long encountered disagreements, trials, and evils they had not anticipated.

items.ar: ثم أرشدهم ﷺ إلى ما يلزمونه عند هذا الاختلاف، فقال: (فَعَلَيكُم بِسَّنتي) أي الزموا سنتي، والمراد بالسنة هنا: الطريقة التي هو عليها، فلا تبتدعوا في دين الله عزّ وجل ما ليس منه،ولا تخرجوا عن شريعته.
items.tr: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, then directed them to what they must adhere to amid this disagreement: 'You must follow my Sunnah (way).' Sunnah here means the way he followed. Do not introduce into Allah's religion what is not part of it or depart from His law.

items.ar: قوله: ( وَسُنَّةِ الخُلَفَاءِ الرَاشِدين) الخلفاء الذين يخلفون رسول الله ﷺ في أمته، وعلى رأسهم أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه.
items.tr: His words, 'And the Sunnah (way) of the rightly guided caliphs': these are the caliphs who succeed the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, in leading his community, foremost among them Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him.

items.ar: فإن أبا بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه هو الخليفة الأول لهذه الأمة، نص النبي ﷺ على خلافته نصاً يقرب من اليقين، وعامله بأمور تشير إلى أنه الخليفة بعده.
items.tr: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was this community's first caliph. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, indicated his succession in terms approaching certainty, and dealt with him in ways indicating that he would be the caliph after him.

items.ar: ثم الخليفة من بعده عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه لأنه أولى الناس بالخلافة بعد أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه فإنهما صاحبا رسول الله ﷺ وكان كثيراً ما يقول: ذهبت أنا وأبو بكر وعمر، وجئت أنا وأبو بكر وعمر،فرأى أبو بكر رضي الله عنه أن أحق الناس بالخلافة عمر رضي الله عنه.
items.tr: The caliph after him was Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, because he had the strongest claim to the caliphate after Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. They were both companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, who often said: 'I, Abu Bakr, and Umar went,' and 'I, Abu Bakr, and Umar came.' Abu Bakr therefore considered Umar to have the strongest claim to the caliphate.

items.ar: وخلافة عمر رضي الله عنه ثابتة شرعاً لأنها وقعت من خليفة،ثم صارت الخلافة لعثمان رضي الله عنه بمشورة معروفة رتبها عمر رضي الله عنه، ثم صارت بعد ذلك لعلي رضي الله عنه هؤلاء هم الخلفاء الراشدون لا إشكال فيهم.
items.tr: Umar's caliphate, may Allah be pleased with him, was established legitimately because he was appointed by a caliph. The caliphate then passed to Uthman through the well-known consultation arranged by Umar, and afterward to Ali, may Allah be pleased with them. These are the rightly guided caliphs, about whom there is no dispute.

items.ar: وقوله: (المهديين) صفة مؤكدة لما سبق، لأنه يلزم من كونهم راشدين أن يكونوا مهديين، إذ لا يمكن رشد إلا بهداية،وعليه فالصفة هنا ليست صفة احتراز ولكنها صفة توكيد وبيان علة،يعني أنهم رشدوا لأنهم مهديون.
items.tr: His words, 'Guided,' reinforce what precedes them. Being rightly directed necessarily entails being guided, because right direction is impossible without guidance. This description therefore does not exclude anyone from the preceding description; it emphasizes it and explains its reason: they were rightly directed because they were guided.

items.ar: وقوله: (عَضُّوا عَلَيهَا) أي على سنتي وسنة الخلفاء (بالنَّوَاجِذِ) وهي أقصى الأضراس ومن المعلوم أن السنة ليست جسماً يؤكل،لكن هذا كناية عن شدة التمسك بها،أي أن الإنسان يتمسك بهذه السنة حتى يعض عليها بأقصى أضراسه.
items.tr: His words, 'Bite onto it,' mean onto my Sunnah (way) and that of the caliphs. 'With your molars' means the rearmost teeth. Obviously the Sunnah is not a physical object to be eaten. This expresses holding firmly to it, as though a person held it so tightly that he bit onto it with his rearmost molars.

items.ar: وقوله: (وَإيَّاكُم) لما حث على التمسك بالسنة حذر من البدعة.
items.tr: His words, 'Beware': after urging adherence to the Sunnah (way), he warned against bidah (religious innovation).

items.ar: وقوله: (وَإيَّاكُم وَمُحدَثَاتِ الأُمور) أي اجتنبوها،والمراد بالأمور هنا الشؤون، والمراد بالشؤون شؤون الدين،لا المحدثات في أمور الدنيا،لأن المحدثات في أمور الدنيا منها ما هو نافع فهو خير،ومنها ما هو ضار فهو شر،لكن المحدثات في أمور الدين كلها شر، ولهذا قال: "فَإِنَّ كُلَّ مُحدَثَةٍ بِدعَة" لأنها ابتدعت وأنشئت من جديد.
items.tr: His words, 'Beware of newly introduced matters,' mean avoid them. 'Matters' here means affairs of religion, not innovations in worldly affairs. Some worldly innovations are beneficial and therefore good; others are harmful and therefore evil. But innovations in religious affairs are all evil. Thus he said: 'Every newly introduced matter is a bidah (religious innovation),' because it has been invented and newly originated.

items.ar: قوله: (كُل بِدعَةٍ ضَلالَة) أي كل بدعة في دين الله عزّ وجل فهي ضلالة.
items.tr: His words, 'Every bidah (religious innovation) is misguidance,' mean that every innovation in Allah's religion is misguidance.

items.ar: العِرْبَاضُ بن سارية السلمي من أعيان أهل الصفة، سكن حمص. وهو أحد البكائين الذين ورد فيهم في القرآن: ﴿وَلَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ إِذَا مَا أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ قُلْتَ لَا أَجِدُ مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ تَوَلَّوْا وَأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ حَزَنًا أَلَّا يَجِدُوا مَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾
items.tr:
Al-Irbad ibn Sariyah as-Sulami was one of the distinguished people of As-Suffah. He settled in Hims. He was one of those who wept, about whom the Quran says: وَلَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ إِذَا مَا أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ قُلْتَ لَا أَجِدُ مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ تَوَلَّوْا وَأَعْيُنُهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ حَزَنًا أَلَّا يَجِدُوا مَا يُنْفِقُونَ [Full-verse context (9:92):
Nor [is there blame] upon those who, when they came to you for you to take them along, you said, "I can find nothing upon which to carry you."[497] They turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they could not find something to spend [for the cause of Allāh].
[497] No mounts or even shoes were available.]

items.ar: روى أحمد في مسنده عن عبد الرحمن بن عمرو السلمي، وحجر بن حجر، قالا: أتينا العرباض بن سارية. وهو ممن نزل فيه: (وَلَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ إِذَا مَا أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ قُلْتَ لَا أَجِدُ مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ) فسلمنا، وقلن: أتيناك زائرين وعائدين ومقتبسين. فقال: صلى بنا رسول الله الصبح ذات يوم، ثم أقبل علينا، فوعظنا موعظة بليغة ذرفت منها العيون، ووجلت منها القلوب، فقيل: يا رسول الله، كأن هذه موعظة مودع، فماذا تعهد إلينا؟ قال: أوصيكم بتقوى الله، والسمع والطاعة وإن عبْدًا حبشيًّ. فإنه من يعِشْ منكم بعدي، فسَيَرى اختلافًا كثير. فعليكم بسنتي وسنة الخلفاء الراشدين المهديين، تمسكوا بها، وعضوا عليها بالنواجذ. وإياكم ومحدثات الأمور ; فإن كل محدثة بدعة وكل بدعة ضلالة.
items.tr:
Ahmad narrated in his Musnad from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Amr as-Sulami and Hujr ibn Hujr, who said: We came to Al-Irbad ibn Sariyah, one of those about whom the following was revealed: وَلَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ إِذَا مَا أَتَوْكَ لِتَحْمِلَهُمْ قُلْتَ لَا أَجِدُ مَا أَحْمِلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ [Full-verse context (9:92):
Nor [is there blame] upon those who, when they came to you for you to take them along, you said, "I can find nothing upon which to carry you."[497] They turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they could not find something to spend [for the cause of Allāh].
[497] No mounts or even shoes were available.]. We greeted him and said: We have come to visit you, enquire after your health and learn from you. He said: صلى بنا رسول الله الصبح ذات يوم، ثم أقبل علينا، فوعظنا موعظة بليغة ذرفت منها العيون، ووجلت منها القلوب، فقيل: يا رسول الله، كأن هذه موعظة مودع، فماذا تعهد إلينا؟ قال: أوصيكم بتقوى الله، والسمع والطاعة وإن عبْدًا حبشيًّ. فإنه من يعِشْ منكم بعدي، فسَيَرى اختلافًا كثير. فعليكم بسنتي وسنة الخلفاء الراشدين المهديين، تمسكوا بها، وعضوا عليها بالنواجذ. وإياكم ومحدثات الأمور ; فإن كل محدثة بدعة وكل بدعة ضلالة. [The Messenger of Allah led us in the dawn prayer one day, then turned towards us and delivered an eloquent exhortation that made eyes shed tears and hearts tremble. Someone said: Messenger of Allah, this seems to be a farewell exhortation. What do you instruct us to do? He said: I counsel you to have taqwa (mindfulness) of Allah, and to hear and obey, even if an Abyssinian slave is in authority. Whoever among you lives after me will see much disagreement. Adhere to my Sunnah (way) and the way of the rightly guided, well-directed caliphs. Hold firmly to it and bite onto it with your molars. Beware of newly introduced matters, for every newly introduced matter is a bidah (religious innovation), and every innovation is misguidance.]

items.ar: ويروى عن أبي الفيض أنه قال: سمعت عمر أبا حفص الحمصي قال: أعطى معاوية المقدام حمارا من المغنم فقال له العرباض بن سارية: ما كان لك أن تأخذه وما كان له أن يعطيك كأني بك في النار تحمله على عنقك فرده.
items.tr: It is related from Abu al-Fayd that he said: I heard Umar Abu Hafs al-Himsi say: Muawiyah gave al-Miqdam a donkey from the spoils. Al-Irbad ibn Sariyah told him: 'You had no right to take it, and he had no right to give it to you. It is as though I see you in the Fire carrying it on your neck.' So he returned it.

items.ar: قال محمد بن عوف: كان قديم الإسلام جدا، وقال خليفة: مات في فتنة ابن الزبير، وقال أبو مسهر: مات بعد ذلك سنة خمس وسبعين.
items.tr: Muhammad ibn Awf said: 'He embraced Islam very early.' Khalifah said: 'He died during the turmoil of Ibn al-Zubayr.' Abu Mushir said: 'He died later than that, in the year seventy-five.'

items.ar: ويظن أنه دفن في قرية كفرلاها في محافظة حمص وله مقام وجامع يزوره أهل القرية ومقامه على بعد 27 كم من مدينة حمص
items.tr: He is thought to be buried in the village of Kafr Laha in Homs Governorate. He has a shrine and a mosque visited by the villagers; his shrine is 27 km from the city of Homs.

items.ar: هِمَمُ الصحابة رضي الله عنهم عالية، فلم يقل:أخبرني بعمل أكسب فيه العشرة عشرين أو ثلاثين أو ما أشبه بذلك، بل قال: (أَخبِرنِي بِعَمَلٍٍ يُدخِلُني الجَنَّةَ وَيُبَاعدني من النارَ) أي يكون سبباً لدخول الجنة والبعد عن النار.
items.tr: The aspirations of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were lofty. He did not say: tell me of a deed by which I can turn ten into twenty or thirty, or something similar. Rather, he said: 'Tell me of a deed that will admit me to Paradise and keep me away from the Fire,' meaning a cause of entering Paradise and being kept away from the Fire.

items.ar: فقال النبي ﷺ (لَقَد سَأَلتَ عَنْ عَظيمٍ) أي والله عظيم، هذه هي الحياة، أن تدخل الجنة وتبتعد عن النار، هذا هو الفوز والفلاح، قال الله عزّ وجل: (فَمَنْ زُحْزِحَ عَنِ النَّارِ وَأُدْخِلَ الْجَنَّةَ فَقَدْ فَازَ) ولهذا وصفه النبي ﷺ بأنه عظيم، ولكن الحمد لله.قوله: (وَإِنهُ ليَسيرٌ عَلى مِنْ يَسرَهُ اللهُ عَلَيه) - اللهم يسره علينا يا رب العالمين - وصدق النبي ﷺ فإن الدين الإسلامي مبني على اليسر، قال الله تعالى: (يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ) ومبني على السمح قال النبي ﷺ لأصحابه وهو يبعثهم إلى الجهات: (يَسِّروا ولا تُعَسِّروا، بَشِّروا وَلاَ تُنَفِّروا)، (فَإِنَمَا بُعِثتُم مُيَسِّرين وَلَم تُبعَثوا مُعَسِّرين) وقال ﷺ: (إِنَّ هذا الدينُ يُسر، وَلَن يُشَاد الدينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ) فهو يسير لكن لمن يسره الله عليه، ثم شرح ذلك فقال:
items.tr:
The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: لَقَد سَأَلتَ عَنْ عَظيمٍ [You have asked about something momentous.] Indeed, by Allah, it is momentous. This is life: to enter Paradise and be kept away from the Fire. This is success and prosperity. Allah, mighty and majestic, says: فَمَنْ زُحْزِحَ عَنِ النَّارِ وَأُدْخِلَ الْجَنَّةَ فَقَدْ فَازَ [Full-verse context (3:185):
Every soul will taste death, and you will only be given your [full] compensation on the Day of Resurrection. So he who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire]. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion.]. That is why the Prophet described it as momentous. Yet, praise be to Allah, his statement is: وَإِنهُ ليَسيرٌ عَلى مِنْ يَسرَهُ اللهُ عَلَيه [It is easy for anyone for whom Allah makes it easy.] O Allah, make it easy for us, Lord of all worlds. The Prophet spoke the truth: the Islamic religion is founded on ease. Allah Most High says: يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ [Full-verse context (2:185):
The month of Ramaḍān [is that] in which was revealed the Qur’ān, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights [the crescent of] the month,[66] let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allāh intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allāh for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful.
[66] Also, "whoever is present during the month."]. It is also founded on forbearance. The Prophet said to his companions when sending them to different regions: يَسِّروا ولا تُعَسِّروا، بَشِّروا وَلاَ تُنَفِّروا [Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not drive people away.], and فَإِنَمَا بُعِثتُم مُيَسِّرين وَلَم تُبعَثوا مُعَسِّرين [You were sent to make things easy, not to make them difficult.]. He also said: إِنَّ هذا الدينُ يُسر، وَلَن يُشَاد الدينَ أَحَدٌ إِلاَّ غَلَبَهُ [This religion is easy, and no one makes the religion excessively hard upon himself without it overcoming him.]. It is easy, but for those for whom Allah makes it easy. Then he explained this, saying:

items.ar: (تَعبُدَ اللهَ) بمعنى تتذلل له بالعبادة حباً وتعظيماً، فبالمحبة تفعل الطاعات، وبالتعظيم تترك المعاصي.
items.tr: 'Worship Allah' means humble yourself before Him in worship, with love and reverence. Love leads you to perform acts of obedience, and reverence leads you to abandon sins.

items.ar: (لا تُشرِك بِهِ شيئاً) أي شي يكون حتى الأنبياء، بل الأنبياء ما جاؤوا إلا لمحاربة الشرك، فلا تشرك به شيئاً لا ملكاً مقرباً،ولا نبياً مرسلاً،
items.tr: 'Do not associate anything with Him': anything whatsoever, even the prophets. Indeed, the prophets came only to combat shirk (associating partners with Allah). Associate nothing with Him, neither an angel brought near nor a messenger sent.

items.ar: قال: (وَتُقيم الصَلاةَ، وَتُؤتي الزكَاةَ، وَتَصوم رَمَضَانَ،وَتَحُج البَيتَ) هذه أركان الإسلام الخمسة.
items.tr: He said: 'Establish prayer, give zakah (obligatory alms), fast Ramadan, and perform Hajj (pilgrimage) to the House.' These are the five pillars of Islam.

items.ar: ثم قال: (أَلاَ أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى أَبوَابِ الخَيرِ) أبواب أي مسائل، وأبواب تستعمل في الباب الذي يفتح للداخل والخارج، وتستعمل في المسائل، ومن هذا قول العلماء في مؤلفاتهم:هذا الباب في كذا وكذا. وقول المحدثين: لا يصح في هذا الباب شيء، أي لا يصح في هذه المسألة شيء.
items.tr: He then said: 'Shall I direct you to the doors of goodness?' 'Doors' means matters. The word is used for a door opened for someone entering or leaving, and also for subjects. Thus scholars say in their writings: this chapter concerns such and such; hadith scholars say: nothing authentic has been reported in this chapter, meaning on this subject.

items.ar: فقوله: (أَبوَابِ الخَيرِ) أي مسائل الخير، ويجوز أن يكون المراد به الباب المعروف الذي يكون منه الدخول والخروج.
items.tr: His words, 'The doors of goodness,' mean matters of goodness. They may also mean doors in the familiar sense, through which one enters and leaves.

items.ar: (أَلا أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى أَبوَابِ الخَيرِ) والجواب: بلى، لكن حذف للعلم به، لأنه لابد أن يكون الجواب بلى.
items.tr: 'Shall I direct you to the doors of goodness?' The answer is yes, but it is omitted because it is understood: the answer must be yes.

items.ar: قال: (الصَّومُ جنةٌ) أي مانع يمنع صاحبه في الدنيا ويمنع صاحبه في الآخرة.
items.tr: He said: 'Fasting is a shield,' meaning a barrier that protects the person fasting in this world and in the Hereafter.

items.ar: أما في الدنيا فإنه يمنع صاحبه من تناول الشهوات الممنوعة في الصوم، وأما في الآخرة فهو جُنَّةٌ من النار، يقيك من النار يوم القيامة.
items.tr: In this world it restrains him from indulging the desires prohibited during fasting. In the Hereafter it is a shield against the Fire, protecting you from it on the Day of Resurrection.

items.ar: والصوم: التعبد لله تعالى بالإمساك عن المفطرات من طلوع الفجر إلى غروب الشمس.
items.tr: Fasting means worshipping Allah by refraining from things that invalidate the fast, from dawn until sunset.

items.ar: قوله: (وَالصَّدَقَة تُطفِىء الخَطيئَة كَمَا يُطفِىء المَاءُ النَّارَ) الصدقة مطلقاً سواء الزكاة الواجبة أو التطوع،و سواء كانت قليلة أو كثيرة.
items.tr: His words, 'Charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire,' concern charity generally: obligatory zakah (alms) or voluntary giving, whether little or much.

items.ar: قوله: (تُطفِئ الخَطيئَة) أي خطيئة بني آدم، وهي المعاصي.
items.tr: His words, 'Extinguishes sin,' mean the sins of the children of Adam: their acts of disobedience.

items.ar: قوله: (كَمَا يُطفِئ المَاءُ النَّارَ) والماء يطفئ النار بدون تردد، فشبه النبي ﷺ الأمر المعنوي بالأمر الحسي.
items.tr: His words, 'As water extinguishes fire': water certainly extinguishes fire. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, thus compared something intangible to something perceptible.

items.ar: قوله: (وَصَلاةُ الرّجُل في جَوفِ اللَّيلِ) هذه معطوفة على قوله "الصدقة" أي وصلاة الرجل في جوف الليل تطفئ الخطيئة، وجوف الليل وسطه كجوف الإنسان.
items.tr: His words, 'And a man's prayer in the depths of the night,' are linked grammatically to 'charity': a man's prayer in the depths of the night also extinguishes sin. The depths of the night mean its middle, like the interior of a person's body.

items.ar: ثم تلا ﷺ: (تَتَجَافَى جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ * فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ*) تلا أي قرأ (تَتَجَافَى جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ) هذا في وصف المؤمنين، أي أنهم لا ينامون (يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً) إن ذكروا ذنوبهم خافوا، وإن ذكروا فضل الله طمعوا، فهم بين الخوف و الرجاء، (وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ) (من) هنا إما أن تكون للتبعيض والمعنى ينفقون بعضها، أو تكون للبيان،والمعنى ينفقون مما رزقهم الله عزّ وجل قليلاً كان أو كثيراً (فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ)، استشهد النبي ﷺ بهذه الآية على فضيلة قيام الليل،ثم قال: (أَلاَ أُخبِرُكَ بِرَأَسِ الأَمرِ،وَعَمودِهِ،وذِروَةِ سِنَامِهِ) ثلاثة أشياء:
items.tr:
Then he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited: تَتَجَافَى جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ * فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ* [Full-verse context (32:16):
Their sides part [i.e., they arise] from [their] beds; they supplicate their Lord in fear and aspiration, and from what We have provided them, they spend.[1174]
[1174] In the cause of Allāh.

Full-verse context (32:17):
And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes [i.e., satisfaction] as reward for what they used to do.]. 'Recited' means read. تَتَجَافَى جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ [Full-verse context (32:16):
Their sides part [i.e., they arise] from [their] beds; they supplicate their Lord in fear and aspiration, and from what We have provided them, they spend.[1174]
[1174] In the cause of Allāh.]: this describes the believers, meaning they do not sleep. يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً [Full-verse context (32:16):
Their sides part [i.e., they arise] from [their] beds; they supplicate their Lord in fear and aspiration, and from what We have provided them, they spend.[1174]
[1174] In the cause of Allāh.]: when they remember their sins, they fear, and when they remember Allah's bounty, they hope; they are between fear and hope. وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ [Full-verse context (32:16):
Their sides part [i.e., they arise] from [their] beds; they supplicate their Lord in fear and aspiration, and from what We have provided them, they spend.[1174]
[1174] In the cause of Allāh.]: min (from) here either indicates a portion, meaning they spend some of it, or clarifies the source, meaning they spend from what Allah, mighty and majestic, has provided them, whether little or much. فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ مَا أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ مِنْ قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ جَزَاءً بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ [Full-verse context (32:17):
And no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes [i.e., satisfaction] as reward for what they used to do.]. The Prophet cited this verse as evidence of the virtue of night prayer, then said: أَلاَ أُخبِرُكَ بِرَأَسِ الأَمرِ،وَعَمودِهِ،وذِروَةِ سِنَامِهِ [Shall I tell you of the head of the matter, its pillar and the peak of its hump?] Three things:

items.ar: (قُلتُ: بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ الله، قَالَ: رَأَسُ الأَمرِ الإِسلام) أمر الإنسان الذي من أجله خُلِقَ، رأسه الإسلام، أي أن يسلم لله تعالى ظاهراً وباطناً بقلبه وجوارحه.
items.tr: 'I said: Yes, Messenger of Allah. He said: The head of the matter is Islam.' The head of the human affair for which a person was created is Islam: submitting to Allah outwardly and inwardly, with the heart and the limbs.

items.ar: قوله: (وَعَمودِهِ الصلاة) أي عمود الإسلام الصلوات،والمراد بها الصلوات الخمس، وعمود الخيمة ما تقوم عليه، وإذا أزيل سقطت.
items.tr: His words, 'And its pillar is prayer,' mean that the pillar of Islam is prayer, specifically the five prayers. A tent's pole is what supports it; if it is removed, the tent collapses.

items.ar: قوله: (وَذِروَةِ سِنَامِهِ الجِهَاد في سَبيلِ الله) ذكر الجهاد أنه ذروة السنام،لأن الذروة أعلى شيء، قال الله تعالى: (وَلا تَهِنُوا وَلا تَحْزَنُوا وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ)
items.tr:
His statement: وَذِروَةِ سِنَامِهِ الجِهَاد في سَبيلِ الله [The peak of its hump is jihad (striving) in Allah's cause.] He described jihad as the peak of the hump because the peak is the highest part. Allah Most High says: وَلا تَهِنُوا وَلا تَحْزَنُوا وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ [Full-verse context (3:139):
So do not weaken and do not grieve, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers.]

items.ar: وقوله: (الجهاد) يعني في سبيل الله عزّ وجل والجهاد في سبيل الله بينه النبي ﷺ أتم بيان، فقد سئل عن الرجل يقاتل حمية، ويقاتل شجاعة، ويقاتل ليرى مكانه، أي ذلك في سبيل الله؟ فقال: (مَن قَاتَلَ لِتَكونَ كَلِمَةُ اللهِ هي العُليَا فَهوَ في سَبيلِ اللهِ)
items.tr: His words, 'Jihad (striving),' mean in Allah's cause. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, explained jihad in Allah's cause fully. He was asked about a man who fights out of partisanship, one who fights to show courage, and one who fights to have his position recognized: which is in Allah's cause? He said: 'Whoever fights so that Allah's word is supreme is in Allah's cause.'

items.ar: ثم قال: (أَلاَ أُخبِرُكَ بِمَلاك ذَلكَ كُله) ملاك الشيء ما يملك به، والمعنى ما تملك به كل هذا.
items.tr: He then said: 'Shall I tell you what controls all of that?' The controlling element of something is that by which it is held in control. The meaning is: what enables you to control all this.

items.ar: (قُلتُ:بَلَى يَا رَسُول الله، قَالَ: فَأَخذ بِلِسانِهِ وَقَالَ: كُفَّ عَليكَ هَذا) أخذ النبي ﷺ بلسان نفسه وقال: (كُفَّ عَليكَ هَذا) أي لاتطلقه في القيل والقال، وقد تقدم قوله: "مَنْ كَانَ يُؤمِنُ بِاللهِ وَاليَومِ الآخِرِ فَليَقُل خَيرَاً أَو ليَصمُت" فلا تتكلم إلا بخير.
items.tr: 'I said: Yes, Messenger of Allah. He took hold of his tongue and said: Restrain this.' The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, took hold of his own tongue and said: 'Restrain this,' meaning do not let it loose in idle talk. His words have already been mentioned: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.' Speak only good.

items.ar: (قُلتُ: يَا نَبيَّ الله وَإِنَّا لَمؤاخِذونَ بِما نَتَكَلّم بِه) والمعنى:أإنا لمؤاخذون بما نتكلم به؟ يعني أن معاذاً رضي الله عنه تعجب كيف يؤاخذ الإنسان بما يتكلم به.
items.tr: 'I said: Prophet of Allah, will we really be held accountable for what we say?' The meaning is a question: will we be held accountable for our words? Muadh, may Allah be pleased with him, was astonished that a person could be held accountable for what he said.

items.ar: فقال النبي ﷺ حثاً على أن يفهم: (ثَكِلَتكَ أُمُّكَ يَا مُعَاذ) أي فقدتك، وهذه الكلمة يقولها العرب للإغراء والحث،ولا يقصدون بها المعنى الظاهر، وهو أن تفقده أمه،.
items.tr: To urge him to understand, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'May your mother lose you, Muadh!' This means be bereaved of you. The Arabs use this expression to urge and encourage; they do not intend its literal meaning, that his mother should lose him.

items.ar: (وَهَل يَكُبُّ النَّاسَ في النارِ عَلى وجُوهِهم، أَو قَالَ: عَلَى منَاخِرهِم" هذا شك من الراوي) إِلا حَصائدُ أَلسِنَتِهم" أي ما يحصدون بألسنتهم من الأقوال.
items.tr: 'Does anything throw people into the Fire on their faces, or' he said, 'on their noses'—this is uncertainty on the narrator's part—'except the harvests of their tongues?' This means the words they reap with their tongues.

items.ar: لما قال هذا الكلام اقتنع معاذ رضي الله عنه وعرف أن ملاك الأمر كف اللسان،لأن اللسان قد يقول الشرك، وقد يقول الكفر، وقد يقول الفحشاء، فهو ليس له حد.
items.tr: When he said this, Muadh, may Allah be pleased with him, was convinced and understood that restraining the tongue controls the whole matter. The tongue may utter shirk (associating partners with Allah), disbelief, or obscenity; it has no limit.

items.ar: قوله: (فَرَضَ) أي أوجب قطعاً، لأنه من الفرض وهو القطع.
items.tr: His word, 'Prescribed,' means imposed decisively as an obligation, because the Arabic root of fard (obligation) means cutting.

items.ar: قوله: (فَرَضَفَرَائِضَ) مثل الصلوات الخمس، والزكاة، والصيام،والحج،وبر الوالدين، وصلة الأرحام، ومالا يحصى.
items.tr: His words, 'Prescribed obligations,' include the five prayers, zakah (obligatory alms), fasting, Hajj (pilgrimage), dutifulness to parents, maintaining kinship ties, and countless others.

items.ar: قوله: (فَلاتُضَيِّعُوهَا) أي تهملوها فتضيع، بل حافظوا عليها.
items.tr: His words, 'Do not neglect them,' mean do not disregard them so that they are lost; rather, preserve them.

items.ar: قوله: (وَحَدَّحُدودَاًفَلاتَعتَدوها) الحد في اللغة المنع، ومنه الحد بين الأراضي لمنعه من دخول أحد الجارين على الآخر، وفي الاصطلاح قيل:إن المراد بالحدود الواجبات والمحرمات.
items.tr: His words, 'Set limits, so do not transgress them': linguistically, a limit means prevention. Thus the boundary between properties prevents either neighbor from encroaching on the other. In technical usage, it has been said that 'limits' means obligations and prohibitions.

items.ar: فالواجبات حدود لا تُتعدى، والمحرمات حدود لا تقرب.
items.tr: Obligations are limits not to be transgressed; prohibitions are limits not to be approached.

items.ar: وقال بعضهم: المراد بالحدود العقوبات الشرعية كعقوبة الزنا، وعقوبة السرقة وما أشبه ذلك.
items.tr: Some have said that 'limits' means the prescribed punishments, such as the punishments for zina (unlawful sexual intercourse), theft, and similar offenses.

items.ar: ولكن الصواب الأول،أن المراد بالحدود في الحديث محارم الله عزّ وجل الواجبات والمحرمات، لكن الواجب نقول:لا تعتده أي لاتتجاوزه، والمحرم نقول: لا تقربه، هكذا في القرآن الكريم لما ذكر الله تعالى تحريم الأكل والشرب على الصائم قال: (تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلا تَعْتَدُوهَا) ولما ذكر العدة وما يجب فيها قال: (تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلا تَقرَبُوهَا). [تنبيه: كذا في المطبوع، والذي في المصحف أن آية الصيام (البقرة: ١٨٧) خُتمت بقوله تعالى: ﴿تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا﴾، وآية الطلاق (البقرة: ٢٢٩) خُتمت بقوله تعالى: ﴿تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا﴾، وهو الموافق لتقرير الشيخ رحمه الله.]
items.tr:
The first view, however, is correct: the limits in the hadith mean Allah's inviolable bounds, mighty and majestic, encompassing obligations and prohibitions. Regarding an obligation, we say: do not transgress it, meaning do not go beyond it. Regarding a prohibition, we say: do not approach it. This is how it occurs in the Noble Quran: when Allah Most High mentioned the prohibition on eating and drinking for a fasting person, He said: تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلا تَعْتَدُوهَا [Full-verse context (2:229):
Divorce is twice. Then [after that], either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment. And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them unless both fear that they will not be able to keep [within] the limits of Allāh.[89] But if you fear that they will not keep [within] the limits of Allāh, then there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself. These are the limits of Allāh, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allāh - it is those who are the wrongdoers [i.e., the unjust].
[89] i.e., deal fairly with each other.], and when He mentioned the iddah (waiting period) and its obligations, He said: تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلا تَقرَبُوهَا [Full-verse context (2:187):
It has been made permissible for you the night preceding fasting to go to your wives [for sexual relations]. They are a clothing for you and you are a clothing[67] for them. Allāh knows that you used to deceive yourselves,[68] so He accepted your repentance and forgave you. So now, have relations with them and seek that which Allāh has decreed for you [i.e., offspring]. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the night [i.e., sunset]. And do not have relations with them as long as you are staying for worship in the mosques. These are the limits [set by] Allāh, so do not approach them. Thus does Allāh make clear His verses [i.e., ordinances] to the people that they may become righteous.
[67] Also a source of tranquility and rest.
[68] Prior to this revelation, marital relations were unlawful during nights preceding fasting. Some were unable to refrain and secretly disobeyed, but they did not deceive Allāh.]. [Editor's note: This is how the printed text reads. In the Quran, the fasting verse (al-Baqarah 2:187) concludes with Allah's words: تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا [Full-verse context (2:187):
It has been made permissible for you the night preceding fasting to go to your wives [for sexual relations]. They are a clothing for you and you are a clothing[67] for them. Allāh knows that you used to deceive yourselves,[68] so He accepted your repentance and forgave you. So now, have relations with them and seek that which Allāh has decreed for you [i.e., offspring]. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the night [i.e., sunset]. And do not have relations with them as long as you are staying for worship in the mosques. These are the limits [set by] Allāh, so do not approach them. Thus does Allāh make clear His verses [i.e., ordinances] to the people that they may become righteous.
[67] Also a source of tranquility and rest.
[68] Prior to this revelation, marital relations were unlawful during nights preceding fasting. Some were unable to refrain and secretly disobeyed, but they did not deceive Allāh.], and the divorce verse (al-Baqarah 2:229) concludes with His words: تِلْكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَعْتَدُوهَا [Full-verse context (2:229):
Divorce is twice. Then [after that], either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment. And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them unless both fear that they will not be able to keep [within] the limits of Allāh.[89] But if you fear that they will not keep [within] the limits of Allāh, then there is no blame upon either of them concerning that by which she ransoms herself. These are the limits of Allāh, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allāh - it is those who are the wrongdoers [i.e., the unjust].
[89] i.e., deal fairly with each other.]. This agrees with the Sheikh's explanation, may Allah have mercy on him.]

items.ar: قوله: (وَحَرَّمَ أَشيَاء فَلا تَنتَهِكوهَا) أيفلا تفعلوها، مثل:الزنا، وشرب الخمر، والقذف، وأشياء كثيرة لا تحصى.
items.tr: His words, 'He has forbidden things, so do not violate them,' mean do not do them: for example, zina (unlawful sexual intercourse), drinking wine, qadhf (accusing someone of unlawful sexual intercourse), and countless other things.

items.ar: قوله: (وَسَكَتَ عَنْ أَشيَاء رَحمَةً لَكُمْ غَيرَ نسيَان فَلا تَبحَثوا عَنهَا) سكت عن أشياء أي لم يحرمها ولم يفرضها.
items.tr: His words, 'He has remained silent about things out of mercy for you, not forgetfulness, so do not investigate them': remaining silent about things means He has neither forbidden them nor made them obligatory.

items.ar: قال: سكت بمعنى لم يقل فيها شيئاً، ولا أوجبها ولا حرمها.
items.tr: He said: remaining silent means He has said nothing about them, neither requiring nor forbidding them.

items.ar: وقوله: (غَيْرَ نسيَان) أي أنه عزّ وجل لم يتركها ناسياً لوقوله تعالى: (وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيّاً) ولكن رحمة بالخلق حتى لا يضيق عليهم.
items.tr:
His statement: غَيْرَ نسيَان [Without forgetfulness.] This means that He, mighty and majestic, did not leave them unmentioned out of forgetfulness, because He Most High says: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيّاً [Full-verse context (19:64):
[Gabriel said],[821] "And we [angels] descend not except by the order of your Lord. To Him belongs that before us and that behind us and what is in between. And never is your Lord forgetful -
[821] In answer to the Prophet's wish that Gabriel would visit him more often.]. Rather, it was out of mercy towards creation, so as not to make things restrictive for them.

items.ar: قوله: (فَلا تَبحَثوا عَنهَا) أي لا تسألوا، مأخوذ من بحث الطائر في الأرض، أي لا تُنَقِّبُوا عنها،بل دعوها.
items.tr: His words, 'Do not investigate them,' mean do not ask. The expression derives from a bird scratching in the earth: do not dig into them; leave them alone.

items.ar: الصحابي أبو ثعلبة الخشني جرثوم بن ناشب، وقيل: جرهم بن ناشب، وقيل: ابن ناشم، وقيل: ابن لاشر، وقيل: ابن عمرو، أبو ثعلبة الخشني، وقد اختلف في اسمه واسم أبيه كثيراً، وهو منسوب إلى خشين، بطن من قضاعة.
items.tr: The Companion Abu Thalabah al-Khushani: Jurthum ibn Nashib; also reported as Jurhum ibn Nashib, Ibn Nashim, Ibn Lashir, or Ibn Amr. He was Abu Thalabah al-Khushani. There is considerable disagreement about his name and his father's name. He is affiliated with Khushayn, a clan of Qudaah.

items.ar: شهد الحديبية، وبايع تحت الشجرة بيعة الرضوان، وضرب له رسول الله بسهمه يوم خيبر، وأرسله النبي إلى قومه، فأسلموا، ونزل الشام، ومات أول إمرة معاوية، وقيل: مات أيام يزيد، وقيل: توفي سنة خمس وسبعين، أيام عبد الملك بن مروان.
items.tr: He attended al-Hudaybiyah and gave Bayat al-Ridwan (the pledge of approval) beneath the tree. The Messenger of Allah allotted him a share on the day of Khaybar and sent him to his people, who embraced Islam. He settled in al-Sham. He died early in Muawiyah's rule; it is also said during Yazid's days, or in the year seventy-five, during the rule of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan.

items.ar: قوله: (جَاءَ رَجُلٌ) لم يعين اسمه، ومثل هذا لا حاجة إليه، ولاينبغي أن نتكلف بإضاعة الوقت في معرفة هذا الرجل، وهذا يأتي في أحاديث كثيرة، إلا إذا كان يترتب على معرفته بعينه اختلاف الحكم فلابد من معرفته.
items.tr: His words, 'A man came': his name is not specified. Such information is unnecessary, and we should not labor to waste time identifying this man. This occurs in many hadiths, unless identifying him specifically would change the ruling, in which case his identity must be known.

items.ar: وقوله: (دُلني عَلَى عَمَلٍ إِذَا عَملتُهُ أَحَبَّني الله،وَأَحبَّني النَّاس) هذا الرجل طلب حاجتين عظيمتين، أولهما محبة الله عزّ وجل والثانية محبة الناس.
items.tr: His words, 'Direct me to a deed which, if I do it, Allah will love me and people will love me': this man sought two great things, first Allah's love, and second people's love.

items.ar: فدله النبي ﷺ على عمل معين محدد،فقال: (ازهَد في الدُّنيَا) والزهد في الدنيا الرغبة عنها، وأن لا يتناول الإنسان منها إلا ما ينفعه في الآخرة، وهو أعلى من الورع، لأن الورع: ترك ما يضر من أمور الدنيا، والزهد: ترك مالا ينفع في الآخرة، وترك ما لا ينفع أعلى من ترك ما يضر.
items.tr: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, directed him to a specific deed: 'Practice zuhd (detachment) concerning this world.' Detachment from this world means turning away from it and taking from it only what benefits one in the Hereafter. It is higher than wara (scrupulousness), because scrupulousness means leaving worldly things that harm, whereas detachment means leaving what does not benefit in the Hereafter. Leaving what does not benefit is higher than leaving what harms.

items.ar: وقوله: (يُحِبكَ الله) هو بالجزم على أنه جواب: ازهَد
items.tr: His words, 'Allah will love you,' are in the jussive form in Arabic as the consequence of the command 'Practice detachment.'

items.ar: والدنيا: هي هذه الدار التي نحن فيها، وسميت بذلك لوجهين:
items.tr: Al-dunya (this world) is the abode we are in. It is given this name for two reasons:

items.ar: الوجه الأول: دنيا في الزمن.
items.tr: The first reason: it is nearer in time.

items.ar: الوجه الثاني: دنيا في المرتبة.
items.tr: The second reason: it is lower in rank.

items.ar: فهي دنيا في الزمن لأنها قبل الآخرة، ودنيا في المرتبة لأنها دون الآخرة بكثير جداً، قال النبي ﷺ: "لَمَوضِعُ سوطِ أَحَدِكُم في الجَنَّةِ خَيرٌ مِنَ الدُّنيَا وَمَا فيهَا" وقال النبي ﷺ "ركعَتَا الفَجرِ خَيرٌ مِنَ الدُّنيَا وَمَا فيهَا" إذاً الدنيا ليست بشيء.
items.tr: It is nearer in time because it precedes the Hereafter, and lower in rank because it is far beneath the Hereafter. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'The space occupied by one of your whips in Paradise is better than this world and all it contains.' He also said: 'The two rakahs (units of prayer) before Fajr are better than this world and all it contains.' Thus this world amounts to nothing.

items.ar: وقوله: (وازهَد فيمَا عِندَ النَاس يُحِبكَ النَّاس) أي لا تتطلع لما في أيديهم، ارغب عما في أيدي الناس يحبك الناس، وهذا يتضمن ترك سؤال الناس أي أن لا تسأل الناس شيئاً، لأنك إذا سألت أثقلت عليهم، وكنت دانياً سافلاً بالنسبة لهم،فإن اليد العليا المعطية خير من اليد السفلى الآخذة.
items.tr: His words, 'Be detached from what people possess and people will love you,' mean do not covet what is in their hands. Turn away from what people possess and they will love you. This includes refraining from asking people for things: do not ask them for anything. When you ask, you burden them and become low and inferior in relation to them. The upper, giving hand is better than the lower, receiving hand.

items.ar: هو أبو العباس سهل بن سعد بن مالك بن خالد بن ثعلبة بن حارثة بن عمرو بن الخزرج بن ساعد بن كعب بن الخزرج الأنصاري الساعدي‏. وهناك من قال إن كنيته هي "أبا يحيى"، ولد قبل الهجرة بخمس سنين. ويذكر أنه اسمه في الأصل كان "حزنًا" ولكن الرسول - ﷺ - قام بتغيير ذلك الاسم إلى اسم سهل؛ وذلك لأنّ الرسول - ﷺ - كان يحب الأسماء الطيبة الحسنة والإيجابية، وكان يغير كل الأسماء القبيحة أو التي تحتوي على شرك بالله تعالى، مثل عبد الشمس، وغيرها. لقد أمدّ الله في عمر الصحابي سهل بن سعد، وعاش طويلًا، حتى أنّه أدرك الحجاج في حياته، ويذكر أنّ الحجاج أرسل له ذات يوم، وسأله: لما لم تنصر أمير المؤمنين عثمان؟، فقال له سهل: فعلت، قال له: كذبت، وأمر بأن يختم على عنقه؛ إذلالًا منه له، حتى يبتعد عنه الناس ولا يسمعوا منه. يقول سهل بن سعد الساعدي: خرجت إلى بيت المقدس حتى أتيت دمشق، فوجدت أهله يعلقون الديباج والحجب، والنساء يلعبون في الدف، فقلت: ألأهل الشام عيد لا نعرفه؟ فوجد قومًا يتحدثون، فسألهم ألكم عيد لا نعرفه؟، فقالوا له: يا شيخ نراك غريبًا، فقال: أنا سهل بن سعد، رأيت رسول الله - ﷺ -، وأحمل حديثًا، فقالوا: ما أعجب السماء لم لا تمطر دمًا، والأرض لم تخسف، فقال: ولم هذا؟، قالوا: هذا رأس الحسين يهدى من العراق.
items.tr: He was Abu al-Abbas Sahl ibn Sad ibn Malik ibn Khalid ibn Thalabah ibn Harithah ibn Amr ibn al-Khazraj ibn Said ibn Kab ibn al-Khazraj al-Ansari al-Saidi. Some have said his kunyah (name beginning with Abu) was Abu Yahya. He was born five years before the Hijrah. It is reported that his original name was Hazn, but the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, changed it to Sahl because he liked good, pleasant, positive names and changed ugly names or those involving shirk (associating partners with Allah), such as Abd al-Shams and others. Allah extended Sahl ibn Sad's life, and he lived long enough to encounter al-Hajjaj. It is reported that al-Hajjaj once summoned him and asked: 'Why did you not support the Commander of the Believers, Uthman?' Sahl told him: 'I did.' He replied: 'You lie,' and ordered that a seal be put on his neck to humiliate him, so people would avoid him and not listen to him. Sahl ibn Sad al-Saidi said: 'I set out for Bayt al-Maqdis and reached Damascus. I found its people hanging silk fabrics and curtains, and women playing frame drums. I asked: Do the people of al-Sham have a festival we do not know? I found some people talking and asked them: Do you have a festival we do not know? They said: Old man, you seem a stranger. I said: I am Sahl ibn Sad. I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and transmit hadith. They said: How astonishing that the sky does not rain blood and the earth does not swallow its people! I asked: Why is that? They said: This is al-Husayn's head, being brought as a gift from Iraq.'

items.ar: توفي بالمدينة سنة 88 هـ وقيل بعدها. وهو آخر الصحابة وفاة في المدينة. وقال بعضهم أنّه عاش مائة سنة أو أكثر وعلى هذا يكون توفي سنة ست وتسعين أو بعدها.
items.tr: He died in Madinah in 88 AH, or later according to another account. He was the last Companion to die in Madinah. Some said he lived a hundred years or more; on that basis he would have died in the year ninety-six or later.

items.ar: الحديث بني عليه قاعدة من القواعد الشرعية التي ذكرها أهل العلم واهتموا بها، وفرعوا عنها. والحديث وإن اختلف في وصله وإرساله إلا أن في القرآن ما يدل عليه باللفظ، (لاَ تُضَآرَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا ) (أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّ) في مواضع من هذا النوع. فالضرر منفي ابتداءً ومكافئةً، يعني لا يبتدئ الإنسان بالضرر، ولا يجيب من ضره بالضرر؛ لئلا يسعى إلى ضرر لا ابتداءً ولا مكافئة، لا بمفرده ولا في مقابل من ضره.
items.tr:
This hadith is the basis of one of the principles of Islamic law that scholars have mentioned, given attention to and used to derive further rulings. Although there is disagreement about whether its chain is connected or mursal (missing the companion link), the Quran contains wording that indicates its meaning: لاَ تُضَآرَّ وَالِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِهَا  [Full-verse context (2:233):
Mothers may nurse [i.e., breastfeed] their children two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing [period]. Upon the father is their [i.e., the mothers'] provision and their clothing according to what is acceptable. No person is charged with more than his capacity. No mother should be harmed through her child, and no father through his child. And upon the [father's] heir is [a duty] like that [of the father]. And if they both desire weaning through mutual consent from both of them and consultation, there is no blame upon either of them. And if you wish to have your children nursed by a substitute, there is no blame upon you as long as you give payment according to what is acceptable. And fear Allāh and know that Allāh is Seeing of what you do.] and أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّ [Full-verse context (4:12):
And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child. But if they have a child, for you is one fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they [may have] made or debt. And for them [i.e., the wives] is one fourth if you leave no child. But if you leave a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you [may have] made or debt. And if a man or woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more than two, they share a third,[167] after any bequest which was made or debt, as long as there is no detriment [caused].[168] [This is] an ordinance from Allāh, and Allāh is Knowing and Forbearing.
[167] These shares are divided equally between males and females. The siblings referred to in this verse are from the mother's side only. Those from 
the father or both parents are mentioned in Āyah 176.
[168] This is a condition for any bequest. If it has been violated by the deceased, his bequest is not to be honored, or it may be adjusted by the executor. See 2:182.], in passages of this kind. Harm is negated both as an initial act and as retaliation: a person must not initiate harm or answer someone who harms him with harm, so that he does not pursue harm either initially or in retaliation, neither on his own initiative nor in response to someone who harmed him.

items.ar: فالحديث فيه تحريم الضرر فقوله: (لا ضرر) وهو نفي يراد به النهي، والنهي إذا جاء بصيغة النفي كان أبلغ وأشد؛ لأن هذه الصورة من الشدة والبشاعة بحيث يصح نفيها عن المجتمع الإسلامي. يعني أن الأصل أنها ليست موجودة أصلاً فلا نحتاج إلى النهي عنها، هي منفية أصلاً، يعني لا يتصور أن المجتمع المسلم، أو مسلمين بينهم يحصل مثل هذا.
items.tr: The hadith prohibits harm. 'There is no harm' is a negation intended as a prohibition. A prohibition expressed as a negation is more emphatic and forceful, because this conduct is so severe and ugly that it can be denied of an Islamic society. The premise is that it does not exist at all, so there is no need to forbid it: it is fundamentally negated. In other words, it is inconceivable that such conduct should occur in a Muslim society or among Muslims.

items.ar: أبو سعيد الخدري: هو سعد بن مالك بن سنان بن ثعلبة بن عبيد بن الأبجر بن عوف بن الحارث بن الخزرج من الصحابة، وهو من ذرية الخزرج الأكبر فقيل له الخزرجي، وهو من الأنصار. أمه أنيسة بنت أبي حارثة من بني عدي النجار. اعتنق أبو سعيد الإسلام باكرا، فكان من الذين أسلموا قبل سن البلوغ.
items.tr: Abu Said al-Khudri was Sad ibn Malik ibn Sinan ibn Thalabah ibn Ubayd ibn al-Abjar ibn Awf ibn al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, one of the Companions. He was descended from al-Khazraj al-Akbar and was therefore called al-Khazraji. He belonged to the Ansar. His mother was Anisah bint Abi Harithah of Banu Adi al-Najjar. Abu Said embraced Islam early, before reaching puberty.

items.ar: استشهد أبوه مالك في معركة أحد، وشارك أبو سعيد في معركة الخندق، وبيعة الرضوان. ويعد من رواة الحديث، فقد روى أبو سعيد 1،170 حديثًا، اتفق البخاري ومسلم على ثلاثة وأربعين، وانفرد البخاري بستة عشر حديثًا، ومسلم باثنين وخمسين. لم يسمح له النبي بالقتال في غزوة أحد لصغر سنه. كان يعظ الخلفاء ويخلص لهم في النصيحة، توفي سنة 74هـ.
items.tr: His father Malik was martyred at Uhud. Abu Said participated in al-Khandaq and Bayat al-Ridwan (the pledge of approval). He was a hadith narrator, transmitting 1,170 hadiths. Al-Bukhari and Muslim both reported forty-three of them; al-Bukhari alone reported sixteen, and Muslim alone fifty-two. The Prophet did not permit him to fight at Uhud because of his young age. He admonished the caliphs and sincerely advised them. He died in 74 AH.

items.ar: قوله: (لَو يُعطَى) المعطي هو من له حق الإعطاء كالقاضي مثلاً والمصلح بين الناس.
items.tr: His words, 'If people were given': the giver is someone with the authority to give, such as a judge or someone reconciling people.

items.ar: وقوله: (بِدَعوَاهُم) أي بادعائهم الشيء،سواء كان إثباتاً أو نفياً.
items.tr: His words, 'On the basis of their claims,' mean their assertion of something, whether an affirmation or a denial.

items.ar: قوله: (لادعى) هذا جواب "لَو"
items.tr: His words, 'Would claim,' form the consequence of the conditional 'if.'

items.ar: قوله: (لادعَى رِجَال) المراد بهم الذين لا يخافون الله تعالى،وأما من خاف الله تعالى فلن يدعي ما ليس له من مال أو دم، (أَموَال قَوم) أي بأن يقول هذا لي، هذا وجه.
items.tr: His words, 'Men would claim,' refer to those who do not fear Allah. Those who fear Allah will not claim property or blood to which they have no right. 'The property of other people': one way is to say, 'This is mine.'

items.ar: ووجه آخر أن يقول: في ذمة هذا الرجل لي كذا وكذا، فيدعي ديناً أو عيناً.
items.tr: Another way is to say: 'This man owes me such and such,' claiming a debt or a specific object.

items.ar: قوله: (وَدِمَاءهُم) بأن يقول: هذا قتل أبي، هذا قتل أخي وما أشبه ذلك، أو يقول: هذا جرحني، فإن هذا نوع من الدماء.
items.tr: His words, 'And their blood,' mean saying: this person killed my father, or my brother, and the like; or saying: this person wounded me, for this is a matter of blood as well.

items.ar: قوله: (وَلَكِنِ البَينَةُ) البينة:ما يبين به الحق، وتكون في إثبات الدعوى (عَلَى المُدَعي) (وَاليَمين) أي دفع الدعوى (عَلَى مَنْ أَنكَر).
items.tr: His words, 'But evidence': evidence is what makes the truth clear and establishes the claim. It is 'required of the claimant.' 'And the oath,' to repel the claim, 'is required of the one who denies it.'

items.ar: فهنا مدعٍ ومدعىً عليه، والمدعي: عليه البينة، والمدعى عليه: عليه اليمين ليدفع الدعوى.
items.tr: There are therefore a claimant and a defendant. The claimant must produce evidence; the defendant must swear an oath to repel the claim.

items.ar: قوله: (وَاليَمين عَلَى مَنْ أَنكَر) أي من أنكر دعوى المدعي.
items.tr: His words, 'The oath is required of the one who denies,' mean the person who denies the claimant's allegation.

items.ar: هذا الحديث أصل عظيم في القضاء، وهو قاعدة عظيمة في القضاء ينتفع بها القاضي وينتفع بها المصلح بين اثنين وما إلى ذلك.
items.tr: This hadith is a great foundation and principle of adjudication. Judges benefit from it, as do those reconciling two people and others in similar situations.

items.ar: قوله: (مَنْ) اسم شرط جازم،و: (رأى) فعل الشرط،وجملة (فَليُغَيرْه بَيَدِه) جواب الشرط.
items.tr: The word 'whoever' is a jussive conditional noun in Arabic. 'Sees' is the conditional verb, and 'Let him change it with his hand' is the consequence of the condition.

items.ar: وقوله: (مَنْ رَأَى) هل المراد من علم وإن لم يرَ بعينه فيشمل من رأى بعينه ومن سمع بأذنه ومن بلغه خبر بيقين وما أشبه ذلك، أو نقول: الرؤيا هنا رؤية العين، أيهما أشمل؟
items.tr: His words, 'Whoever sees': does this mean whoever knows, even if he has not seen with his eyes, thus including someone who sees, hears, or receives certain information and the like? Or should we say that seeing here means seeing with the eyes? Which meaning is broader?

items.ar: الجواب:الأول،فيحمل عليه،وإن كان الظاهر الحديث أنه رؤية العين لكن مادام اللفظ يحتمل معنى أعم فليحمل عليه.
items.tr: The answer is the first, and that is how it should be understood. Although the apparent meaning of the hadith is seeing with the eyes, as long as the wording allows a broader meaning it should be understood accordingly.

items.ar: وقوله: (مُنْكَراً) المنكر:هو ما نهى الله عنه ورسوله، لأنه ينكر على فاعله أن يفعله.
items.tr: His word, 'A wrong': munkar (wrongdoing) is what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, because its perpetrator is reproached for doing it.

items.ar: ( فَلْيُغَيِّرْهُ) أي يغير هذا المنكر بيده.
items.tr: 'Let him change it' means change this wrong with his hand.

items.ar: وقوله: (مُنْكَرَاً) لابد أن يكون منكراً واضحاً يتفق عليه الجميع، أي المنكر والمنكر عليه،أو يكون مخالفة المنكر عليه مبينة على قول ضعيف لا وجه له.
